intro: Viewer Foundation is the Bridge's built-in privacy-conscious identity and progression authority. It uses stable platform IDs, never guesses links from names, and stores no chat text.

sections.title: 1. Name and manage progression
sections.description: Choose the name viewers will see, then enable earning. The built-in identity provider remains available when earning is paused.

sections.title: 2. Optional cross-platform account links
sections.description: Add a link only when the creator has verified both stable platform IDs belong to the same person.

sections.title: 3. Chat and consistency
sections.description: A cooldown controls both ordinary chat awards and consistency progress, so rapid repeated messages cannot farm the bonus.

sections.title: 4. Active and lurk time
sections.description: Active time is settled when viewers keep chatting inside the activity window. Lurk time begins with the configured lurk command and settles on their next message or stream-offline event.
sections.notice: Set the active window at least as long as the required active minutes; StreamBridge safely raises it when needed. Repeating !lurk does not reset the original start time. Platforms do not expose a dependable cross-platform list of silent viewers, so merely opening a stream cannot be verified.

sections.title: 5. Community events
sections.description: Choose fixed awards for follows, redemptions, and raids.

sections.title: 6. Support events
sections.description: These are fixed event awards, not monetary conversions. StreamBridge never infers cash value from bits, gifts, or Jewels.

sections.title: 7. Levels and achievements
sections.description: Levels are deterministic. Achievements are derived from point milestones and do not create a second identity store.

sections.title: 8. Privacy and storage limits
sections.description: Least-recently-seen records are removed at the viewer cap. Replay fingerprints expire automatically.
sections.notice: Private state contains one random installation salt, pseudonymous viewer IDs, point totals, levels, bounded activity counters/timestamps, and replay fingerprints. Raw platform IDs appear only in creator-authored account-link settings; they are never copied into runtime state.
